text:
marc (support): FYI — Acme (prod) opened an escalation: after last model rollout they see JSON parse failures in our webhook consumers. They say outputs now have trailing commas and sometimes unquoted keys. Occurred right after the v4.0 rollout. Pasting repro + sample output they sent.

deploy-bot: model-rollout: redwood-mono-4.0 -> deployed in us-west-2 @ 1751204000 :rocket:

tanya (support): Thanks Marc. Can you paste the exact API call they're making (model param + temperature + messages/system)? Also, any examples of the invalid JSON they get?

marc (support): Here is the minimal repro they gave (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{\n    "model": "redwood-mono-4.0",\n    "temperature": 0.0,\n    "messages": [\n      {"role":"system","content":"You are a JSON-only API. Always return valid JSON matching the schema in 'schema'."},\n      {"role":"user","content":"Return an object with keys: \"summary\" (string) and \"issues\" (array of strings)."}\n    ],\n    "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"},"issues":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["summary","issues"]}\n  }'\n```

marc (support): Their parser fails with this error: "JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 3 (char 2)" — and here's the raw output they received from our API (exact bytes):
```json
{ summary: 'Daily pass rate looks good',, "issues": ['none'], }
```

dmitri (eng-ml): That output explains the error — keys unquoted + single quotes + trailing commas. Not a parser issue. Two likely causes: 1) instruction-following drift in the new model causing it to output pseudo-JS objects, or 2) our post-processing/formatter that used to normalize some tokens isn't covering a changed token stream in v4.0.

marc (support): Acme said it was fine before the rollout (they were on v3.9). They pinned to 3.9 and the problem disappears.

dmitri (eng-ml): Can you confirm whether they're using our "structured_output" flag or just relying on natural language instructions? If structured_output=true we can short-circuit with a stricter serializer.

marc (support): They were using only the schema field above + system instruction, no explicit structured_output flag.

tanya (support): Immediate ask from customer: temporary mitigation (pin or bypass) so their downstream doesn't break, and ETA on a fix/rollback.

dmitri (eng-ml): Immediate options: 
- Recommend pin to redwood-mono-3.9-compat (quick, supported).
- Or set temperature=0 and prepend an explicit machine-parsable wrapper prompt: "Output MUST be valid JSON. If you deviate, reply with EXACTLY: {\"error\":\"PARSE_FAILURE\"}." That tends to help but is brittle.
- Longer term: we'll add a strict JSON sanitizer layer in the runtime that validates and reparses model output and either retries decode or falls back to the 3.9 policy.

tanya (support): I've passed the pin option. Customer accepted pin to 3.9 for the short term. Can you do a hotfix to add the sanitizer while we investigate the root cause?

dmitri (eng-ml): I'll prioritize a quick patch: 1) add a strict JSON validator in the response pipeline for any request that includes a "schema" object; 2) if validation fails, automatically retry generation with a forced format instruction and temperature=0; 3) if retry fails, tag the response and emit an event to ops. That should be safe to ship to hosted customers and mitigate this class of regressions.

olivia (cs): Noted — Acme is ok with pin + will wait for the sanitizer. Please keep me posted on roll-forward ETA so I can unblock billing/reg change tickets.

dmitri (eng-ml): Plan: small runtime patch -> canary in us-west-2 tonight -> full rollout tomorrow morning. Will post final rollout ts.

marc (support): Quick repro test I ran locally against a canary with the sanitizer shows the same prompt yields this on failure path (sanitized):
```json
{\"error\":\"PARSE_FAILURE\"}
```
and on success we get tidy output: 
```json
{\"summary\":\"Daily pass rate looks good\",\"issues\":[]}
```

tanya (support): Perfect. I've told Acme to keep the pin for now; they'll flip back once you confirm the canary is green.

dmitri (eng-ml): Update: canary deployed @1751208000. Early logs show ~95% of previously-invalid outputs are now auto-repaired or retried successfully. Rolling to 100% in 90m if no regressions.

olivia (cs): Acme confirmed they tested and see valid JSON now on our canary endpoint. They're happy to schedule the switch back.

marc (support): Closing loop with Acme: we've pinned them to 3.9 for the window and scheduled a post-mortem once rollout is finished. They want notes about how to make their clients more robust (we recommended strict JSON validation client-side + webhook backoff).

dmitri (eng-ml): Follow-up action items: (1) root-cause: tokenization/formatting diff in v4.0 causing reduced adherence to freeform JS->JSON conversion — eng-ml to deep-dive, (2) add sanitizer to runtime (in prod), (3) add a 'structured_output=strict' parameter for customers to opt into stricter enforcement, (4) document best practices in the API docs.

tanya (support): Thanks team — I'll keep this thread pinned for the Acme PM. If anyone needs exact logs or to add to the incident, reply here. :white_check_mark:
